scenes.name: The Rolling Stones
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Andrew Loog Oldham, su Svengali adolescente, los moldeó como los anti-Beatles: groseros y divisivos, «monstruos melenudos del Id adolescente» (tras la multa por orinar contra el muro de un garaje en 1965, puso a Jagger en el titular). En 1965 «(I Can’t Get No) Satisfaction», con su fuzz y su racimo final de «no», expresó una insatisfacción casi cósmica con el consumismo que los había encumbrado; Jagger, culto y elocuente en Charlie Is My Darling de Peter Whitehead, decía que el pop por fin hablaba de levantarse, ir a trabajar y sentirse jodido. «19th Nervous Breakdown» (4 de febrero de 1966), grabado en Los Ángeles al final de una gira de cuarenta fechas, fue la primera gran declaración pop del año: dos guitarras metálicas entrelazadas (Richards y Brian Jones por última vez en un single), ritmo rockabilly maníaco, casi cuatro minutos sobre una pobre niña rica sin salida. Cada single debía superar al anterior en doce semanas. Mientras se codeaban con Anita Pallenberg, Robert Fraser o Christopher Gibbs, Aftermath (abril), entero de composiciones propias, fue el LP del año, aunque en «Stupid Girl» o «Under My Thumb» el desprecio por las mujeres no inquietó a nadie.

podcast.title: Rumored Affair with David Bowie (1990)
podcast.body: A rumor concerning an affair between Mick Jagger and David Bowie was ignited on the Joan Rivers show in 1990 by David's ex-wife, Angela Bowie. Jagger strongly denied the accusation, and David Bowie's lawyer issued a statement calling the implication "an absolute fabrication." The situation was further complicated by rumors that Angela Bowie and Mick Jagger might have had an affair while she was married to Bowie, leading some to believe the Rolling Stones song "Angie" was about her, though others suggested it was coded for David. "Jagger came up swinging, denying everything."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Association with Marianne Faithfull
podcast.body: Mick Jagger is mentioned as having been the partner of Marianne Faithfull. This association placed Faithfull within the influential social circles of prominent artists, including Jim Morrison, during his time in Europe and Paris. "Marian Favour, que fue una persona bastante cercana a Jim Morrison, al resorce a todas estas bandas porque había sido la pareja de Mick Jagger con lo cual estaba metido en todos estos salados y de la época en la que Jim Morrison pasó en Europa y pasó en Paris, pues tuvieron bastante contacto."

podcast.title: Country House Recording Attempt
podcast.body: In 1968, as The Rolling Stones were exploring options for recording on their own terms, an initial plan involved loading recording equipment into a van at Mick Jagger's country house. "The first solution was to record at Mick Jagger's Country House."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Credited on "Bittersweet Symphony"
podcast.body: After Allan Klein gained control of The Verve's "Bittersweet Symphony" rights, he controversially added Mick Jagger and Keith Richards' names to all songwriting credits on the song and The Verve's album Urban Hymns, despite them not composing the sampled string figure. "who then slapped the names Jagger Richards on all the copies of the song and the album Urban Hymns."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Discomfort with Legal Process
podcast.body: Mick Jagger, alongside Keith Richards, expressed their reluctance and lack of desire to be embroiled in the complicated legal proceedings surrounding "Bitter Sweet Symphony." They did not consider their involvement in these disputes to be appropriate. "Tato Mink Jaer como Chris Riches en el pasado han hecho varias declaraciones respecto a todo este proceso legal tan complejo del que se han visto en versos y ellos no tenían ninguna intención de ver si en estos rollos si no lo consideran correcto."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Diva Comparison
podcast.body: The feeling of being treated like a rock star, or "a diva," when driving on a family road trip, with a partner providing snacks and assistance, was likened to the persona of Mick Jagger. "If I ever feel like a diva, if I feel like a Nick Jagger, it's what I'm driving."

podcast.title: Exploring Feminine Side
podcast.body: Mick Jagger's exploration of his feminine side was accepted by mainstream audiences because it was viewed as "theater" or "performance," allowing audiences to enjoy his artistry without confronting personal details. "Mick Jagger was clearly exploring his feminine side."

podcast.title: Grammy Nomination for "Bitter Sweet Symphony"
podcast.body: Mick Jagger, along with Keith Richards and Richard Ashcroft, received a Grammy nomination for "Best Song of the Year" for "Bitter Sweet Symphony." This nomination is a direct consequence of the legal settlement that credited them as composers, despite them not having originally composed the Verve's version of the song. "el Grammy en mejor canción del año y en ese momento acabaron nominados que Dricha sin minchakers por una canción que ni siquiera habían compuesto."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Influenced by Blueberry Hill
podcast.body: Mick Jagger is counted among the notable artists who have cited Fats Domino's "Blueberry Hill" as an influence on their musical work, highlighting the song's enduring impact across different genres and generations. "Blueberry Hill, in particular, has been cited as an influence by everyone from Mick Jagger to Leonard Cohen."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: King of Political Leaders
podcast.body: Mick Jagger is described as the ultimate political leader in music, the absolute political figurehead of The Rolling Stones, responsible for the band's non-creative, strategic, and economic decisions. "es el Rey de los líderes políticos de entrada música, es el absoluto líder político dentro de los Roni Estons."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Only UK Solo Number One
podcast.body: Mick Jagger's duet with David Bowie on "Dancing in the Street" (1985) was his only number one hit in the UK in his career away from The Rolling Stones. This marked a unique solo chart achievement for Jagger. "By the fall of 85, it reached number one in the UK, still the only number one of Mick Jagger's career away from the Rolling Stones by the way."

podcast.title: Relationship with David Bowie
podcast.body: In the early 1970s, Mick Jagger and David Bowie, both known for sexual experimentation, became close friends after a 1973 Bowie concert. They were frequently seen together in public, including clubs, concerts, and even at a Muhammad Ali fight, with one biographer crediting Bowie for introducing Jagger to gay culture. Bowie's backup singer, Aiba Cherry, claimed the two were "sexually obsessed with each other" and she witnessed them having sex, with associates confirming their close relationship during which they "practically lived together for several months." David's ex-wife, Angela Bowie, claimed on the Joan Rivers show in 1990 that she caught them naked and asleep in bed together. "Mick and Dave were really sexually obsessed with each other. Even though I was in bed with them many times, I ended up just watching them have sex. They became very close and practically lived together for several months."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Vocal Expression Controversy
podcast.body: Mick Jagger was one of several artists, including R&B acts, Elvis, The Beatles, Dylan, New Wavers, and rappers, whose vocal expressions were met with decades of criticism following the invention of the microphone. His singing style was seen by purists as part of a "degenerate form of singing," challenging older norms established before amplified vocals. "R&B acts, Elvis, The Beatles, Dylan, Jagger, New Waivers, rappers all the way up to and beyond death medillars."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rice Krispies Jingle (c. 1963-1964)
xref.body: Very early in their career, around 1963 or 1964, The Rolling Stones were commissioned to write a jingle for Rice Krispies cereal. Brian Jones was responsible for writing the music, while Mick Jagger performed the vocals for the advertisement. "Brian Jones wrote the music and Mick Jagger saying this."

xref.title: Naked in Bed with Mick Jagger – Angela Bowie's 1990 TV Claim, Denied Then Partially Walked Back
xref.body: On May 4, 1990, David Bowie's ex-wife Angela appeared on the Joan Rivers Show, newly freed from a 10-year gag order after their divorce. She stated on national television: "I caught him in bed with Mick Jagger — and yes, they were naked." Bowie was a professed bisexual during the 1970s. Mick Jagger immediately dismissed the claim as "rubbish," and Bowie's lawyer sent an open letter stating that "any implication that there was ever a gay affair between Mick Jagger and David Bowie is an absolute fabrication." Within a week, Angela was qualifying her statement. By her 1993 autobiography, the account had evolved: she had walked in, assumed they had been having sex, and that was her honest belief, but she had no proof. An additional complication: Angela may have had her own affair with Jagger during the marriage, possibly inspiring the Rolling Stones song "Angie" — or, in another rumor, that "Angie" referred to David himself using a nickname. "Did they spend the night together? Yes. Were they naked? Apparently. Was it sexual? Who knows?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rumored Affair with Mick Jagger (1990)
xref.body: A long-standing rumor regarding an affair between David Bowie and Mick Jagger originated on the Joan Rivers show on May 4, 1990. Angela Bowie, David's ex-wife (married 1970-1980), claimed on the show, after a decade-long gag order from her divorce settlement expired, that she caught them naked in bed together. Bowie had professed bisexuality in the 1970s, which lent some credibility to the story. Mick Jagger vehemently denied the claims, and Bowie's lawyer issued a letter calling any implication of a gay affair an "absolute fabrication." Angela Bowie later revised her story in her 1993 autobiography, stating she "just assumed they were having sex" and lacked proof. "I caught David in bed with Mick Jagger."

xref.title: Keith Richards' 2023 View on Modern Music
xref.body: In 2023, Keith Richards expressed strong disapproval of modern music production techniques, citing the use of "push button drums" and synthesized sounds. He described digital recording as a "one-way toilet," indicating his preference for older, more organic methods of music creation. This sentiment from Richards, who played guitar for Mick Jagger on the song "Man, What a Drag It Is Getting Old," highlights a generational perspective on musical change. "Don't get me going on modern day music, push button drums and everything is synthesized. Digital recording is a one-way toilet."

xref.title: Cocaine Party Story in South of France
xref.body: Ahmet Ertegun recounted a story from when the Rolling Stones were in the South of France, at a party with a bowl of cocaine. When the local chief of police arrived, the band members, including Mick Jagger, disguised the cocaine by smearing it on their faces as if it were powder makeup. "he told me the great story about when, you know, they were in the South of France. There was a bowls of cocaine going around. And the chief of police in the little town where they were all staying comes to the party that they're at."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Copyright Dispute and Loss of Publishing Rights
xref.body: The Verve faced a significant legal battle over their song "Bittersweet Symphony," stemming from a licensed sample. Despite an initial agreement for 50% of earnings, Abkco Music (controlled by Allen Klein) and Andrew Loog Oldham sued, leading to The Verve being forced to surrender 100% of the song's publishing rights, resulting in Mick Jagger and Keith Richards being credited as co-writers and receiving all royalties. "Alright, give us 100% of the money made from this song or we will force you to recall every single copy of the song an album from every store and radio station and whatever worldwide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Flea's Studio Work
xref.body: Flea is considered one of the greatest bass players in the world, leading to his hiring as a studio musician for diverse artists including Alanis Morissette, Mick Jagger, and Johnny Cash. He also played bass on Young MC's hit "Busta Move." "He is so good that he has been hired as a studio musician by everyone from Alannis Morse set to Mick Jagger to Johnny Cash."

xref.title: Initiation of Mobile Recording Studio
xref.body: In 1968, The Rolling Stones decided they wanted the flexibility to record on their own time and in locations of their choosing, leading to an initial attempt to load equipment into a van at Mick Jagger's country house, which sparked the idea for their mobile recording studio. "Back in 1968, the Stones decided they wanted to record on their own time and in places of their own choosing and on their own schedule."

xref.title: Trilobite Species after Keith Richards
xref.body: The same scientists, Adrian and Edgecomb, who found Mick Jagger's trilobite also discovered another species, which they named *parahedulous Richard's Eye*. This name is a tribute to the band's guitarist, Keith Richards, linking him to these ancient creatures. "they called it parahedulous Richard's Eye after Keith Richards."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Trilobite Species after Mick Jagger
xref.body: In 1995, a new species of trilobite, an ancient beetle-like animal, was discovered near Nunavut and named *grottocellus jaggeri*. This naming honors the band's frontman, Mick Jagger, suggesting a possible connection by the discoverer, Adrian and Edgecomb. "it will forever be known as a grottocellus jaggeri after Mick Jagger."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
